interactions.hypothesis: Pace x goalie: pace raises SOG but goals only if the goalie and shot quality convert; use xG-based pace for goals and keep SOG pace for saves/SOG markets.
Penalty expectation: teams' taken rates x opponent drawn rates x crew effect x PP efficiency; each factor is shrunk and the product is a PP-goal expectation.
Team total depends on the opposing goalie confirmed only close to puck drop, so team-total prices should jump on confirmation relative to game total which changes less.
EN and OT inclusion rules change totals: contracts including OT/EN add goals mainly in tied/close games; match the model to wording.

Expected goals equal attempts times conversion, so an extra 5 attempts matter more against a weak goalie than a strong one; additive pace and quality effects misprice games where fast teams face elite goalies and slow teams face weak ones.

Goals per power play flatten with penalty minutes because a minor ends on a goal, and PP1 does most of the work early, so doubling expected penalties adds less than double the PP goals; the effect is larger for strong PP units that score early.

The shootout credit of +1 applies only in regular-season games tied after 65 minutes, so it adds mass to odd totals in proportion to P(tie) and to nothing in the playoffs; half-goal rungs at 5.5 and 6.5 therefore have a season-type-specific probability shift.

When a starter is pulled after several goals, the relief goalie's save rate is lower and the trailing team presses, switching the game into a high-total regime; the right tail of the ladder (9.5 to 11.5) is driven by this regime, not by a larger mean.

Empty-net goals appear only when a one-goal game is still live late; how many arrive depends on the leader score-state mix and on the trailing team pull policy and 6v5 risk, so the count of late goals is a threshold response to the entering lead rather than a smooth function of total pace.

game_total_and_team_total.label: Game total goals and team totals
game_total_and_team_total.mechanism: Expected goals for each team equal shot volume times shot quality times goalie conversion, with an additive special-teams component from expected penalties and an empty-net component from late close-game dynamics. Totals are the sum of two overdispersed counts with mild positive correlation through pace, officiating and style; team totals are single-team versions with goalie and opposing defence dominating. Thresholds at integer and half-goal rungs price tail probabilities requiring dispersion estimates.
game_total_and_team_total.target: Whether total goals (or a team's goals) in the game exceed a threshold under the contract's period and OT scope.

interactions.hypothesis: Saves mean = expected SOG faced x (1 - expected goal probability), but variance is dominated by shot volume and pull risk; combine volume distribution with pull mixture.
Favourite goalies: strong teams concede fewer shots and may lead late; interacting win probability with opponent shooting volume tilts the mean down for favourites.
Unconfirmed starter: the ladder is a mixture across starters with different expected volume (starters vs backup facing the same team), so price jumps on confirmation.
Rink SOG counting bias and opponent attempt volume jointly set official shots faced; venue effects matter more for high-volume opponents.

Expected shots faced is the product of the opponent's shot generation and this defence's allowance, with power-play time as an additional multiplier because PP shot rates are about double 5v5; a high-shot opponent facing a leaky penalty-prone defence compounds all three.

Saves have a different relationship to shots in the full-game and pulled regimes: a pull after four goals truncates the count well below the rung, so the distribution below 25 is a mixture whose weight depends on early goals allowed, and goalie quality moves the pull weight rather than the mean.

Before confirmation the model distribution of saves is a mixture over the two possible goalies; if the backup would face the same volume the mean barely changes and only the save rate differs by tenths of a percentage point, so the confirmation effect is smaller than for goal markets.

Overtime adds a block of shots only when regulation is tied, which shifts the mean by about one shot weighted by the tie probability but moves the probability of crossing 25 more when the base mean is near 24; the effect is largest at the median rung.

A favourite faces fewer shots at even strength because it controls play, but score effects work in the opposite direction once it leads: the trailing team shoots more and later pulls its goalie, so the leader's goalie faces the 6v5 flurry. The net shots-against edge of a favourite is therefore smaller than its shot-share gap and saturates beyond a two-goal lead, while underdog goalies carry more early-pull truncation risk.

goalie_saves.label: Goalie saves thresholds
goalie_saves.mechanism: Saves equal shots on goal faced minus goals against, so the mean is the opponent's expected SOG against this defence adjusted for script, penalties and rink counting. Goalie quality only matters at the margin (a few shots), while volume matters most. The largest tail risks are an early pull (truncating saves) and goalie identity uncertainty before confirmation; overtime adds shots if included.
goalie_saves.target: Whether a goalie records at least k saves; eligibility conditional on the goalie playing per the wording.

parlay_combo.label: Parlay / combo contracts

Positive correlations (team win and own player's points) make the joint probability exceed the product of marginals, negative correlations the opposite, and leg-void rules change the effective payoff. Modelling this requires a game-level simulation that generates all legs from shared latent variables.

Period tie probability is the diagonal of a bivariate count whose total is small, so a shift in total changes tie mass more than a shift in difference; tie, win and spread markets must be priced from the same joint, not marginals.

Hypothesis only: the second-period long change makes defensive-zone line changes harder, so teams that concentrate ice time in top lines may gain or lose more than teams that roll four lines; any effect is conditional on deployment and may be zero.

One extra power play lifts the period's expected goals by a fifth to a quarter of a goal, and the effect is convex because a second PP can follow a goal in the same period; the penalty count distribution and PP efficiency multiply, so uncertain counts fatten the upper tail.

First-period chances against a backup goalie depend on his pregame workload and on the opponent chance quality; the interaction is confined to period one, before score state and line matching dominate, and should not be carried to periods two and three.

Goalie identity and first-minute deployments matter proportionally more than in the full game.
period_markets.target: Outcome within a single 20-minute period (winner including tie handling, goal total, spread, or both teams scoring).

interactions.hypothesis: Teammate comparisons: shared game script and linemates mean correlation reduces difference variance; opposing players have different correlation sign via script.
Tie probability matters for small-count stats: with discrete means small, P(tie) can be large; the rules decide who wins ties.

The correlation between the two players' counts changes sign with pair type: linemates share goals and script so rho is positive and the difference has low variance, whereas opponents share pace but face opposed script so rho is near zero or negative; a pooled correlation misprices both.

Tie mass of the difference is a function of the two marginal means: when both players expect counts near zero (points for depth players, saves with few shots) the tie mass is large and the contract mostly prices P(A>B) against a big atom; as means grow the atom shrinks, so the same mean gap implies a larger win probability for high-volume pairs.

If both players are on the same power-play unit they receive the same power-play opportunities, so penalty-count uncertainty shifts both counts together and mostly cancels in the difference, whereas for players on different units it adds variance of opposite effect; unit overlap decides whether penalty uncertainty matters for the contract.

On a linemate pair the same goal credits both, so points are positively dependent in a way that depends on each player's credit share; for a playmaker versus a shooter the co-credit probability is high and the difference is rarely large.

A lineup change that moves one player down a line or off the PP crosses a threshold in expected TOI that reverses the sign of the expected difference; the priced effect is a step at confirmation time rather than a gradual drift.

interactions.hypothesis: Expected SOG = EV TOI x EV rate + PP TOI x PP rate; PP TOI is uncertain because it depends on the number of penalties drawn, so PP-heavy shooters have fatter right tails.
Block/miss conversion x shooter type: defencemen face higher block rates at the point and forwards' SOG depend on slot volume, so the opponent block rate has different effects by position.

Script x TOI: for a favoured team's star, leading late reduces minutes and shots; for an underdog star, trailing raises both.

Expected SOG rises with the number of power plays, and PP1 shooters convert minutes to shots at several times the even-strength rate, so uncertainty in penalty counts fattens the right tail for PP1 shooters but not for penalty-kill defencemen.

Blocks reduce defencemen's point shots far more than forwards' slot shots, so an opponent with strong blocking suppresses defencemen's SOG more; the opponent block rate should be applied conditional on position and shot origin.

Expected SOG equals team volume times the player's share of volume; a high-share forward against a defence that allows few shots has a mean far below his season average, and share and team volume are not additive.

When the unit's high-volume shooter is absent, remaining skaters' shares rise by the vacated amount in proportion to their usage; the effect is conditional on who is out and on whether the replacement is a shooter or a passer.

Stars on the leading team lose minutes only when the lead reaches about three goals; below that threshold their shot count is unaffected, while trailing teams' stars add shots late, so the response of SOG to lead is a threshold, not linear.

If an arena records shots more generously, the effect scales with the number of attempts that reach the net and applies to home and visiting skaters alike, so it multiplies the player rate rather than adding a constant; the effect should be larger for high-volume shooters.

A coach's vote probability depends on over-performance conditional on adversity: a team beating projection while missing top players is valued above the same delta with a healthy roster, so injuries amplify the narrative only when the team is still above expectation.

Information after the ballot deadline cannot change the vote, so the effect of late-season form on the award is zero beyond the cut-off date, whereas before it each point of final points shifts candidate probabilities; the timing creates a threshold in the usefulness of data.

The Art Ross leader is the maximum over correlated contenders: the league scoring level multiplies every contender and largely cancels in who leads, while games missed are idiosyncratic, so a two-week injury to the favourite transfers probability to the next contenders far more than a league-wide scoring drop does.

General managers voting the Vezina weight wins and save percentage, which depend on team defence and starts share as well as on goalie skill, so a strong goalie behind a weak defence or in a tandem is under-rewarded relative to his GSAx; the effect of GSAx on vote share is conditional on starts and team results.

interactions.hypothesis: Short series amplify variance: the same rating gap yields different series win probabilities depending on goalie quality variance and injuries, so goalie uncertainty interacts with series length.
Regress standings luck before simulation but apply NHL tie-break rules to the simulated points to get seeding right.
A long-term injury changes both rating and its uncertainty; the effect on a championship price compounds across rounds.

Title probability is a convex function of team rating, so rating uncertainty raises the probability of mid-tier teams and lowers that of favourites relative to a point-rating simulation; the effect is strongest early in the season and fades as the posterior tightens.

A seven-game series amplifies single-game randomness and goalie volatility compounds with series length: the same rating gap yields a lower win probability than a constant-p recursion would give once goalie autocorrelation is included.

Regulation wins are the first tiebreaker, so two teams with equal points but different loser-point counts have different qualification odds; the effect arises only at ties and is conditional on the points boundary.

A long-term injury to a key player reduces rating, but a team with cap space and assets can replace part of the loss before the deadline, so the effect on a futures price is conditional on capacity and on the date of the injury.

Seed and division create path differences: a division winner plays a wild card while the other seeds meet inside the division; at the boundary between third seed and wild card, the path regime switches, so marginal points have an outsized effect on conference and Cup odds.

A long winning run needs a strong team AND a soft stretch of schedule (home stand, few back-to-backs, weak opponents); because the league maximum is driven by the single best realised run, rating uncertainty and an easy schedule window multiply in the tail, so a mid-strength team with a long soft stretch can out-price a stronger team with a balanced schedule.

In a four-game tournament the starting goalie's save quality multiplies the effect of skater depth: a deep skater roster with a weak starter loses much of its edge because a single elimination-style final is decided on few goals, so goalie quality carries more weight than in an 82-game season.

inputs.why: Team offensive process is the core of win probability once adjusted for opponent and score effects.
Team defensive process determines opponent shot quality; must be lineup-adjusted for the specific game.
Starter identity moves expected goals against by tenths per game and is the largest same-day information event.
Shrunk GSAx converts a given shot-quality environment into goals against.
Absences of top skaters change both rating and special teams; timing of news matters.
PP/PK matchup alters goals expected, scaled by penalty-rate expectations.
Rest and back-to-back status affect skaters and shift goalie starts to backups.
Home ice advantage is modest but persistent; some rinks also alter measured shot counts.
Short-run goals and record carry shooting and save luck that should be regressed.
Overtime and shootout rules decide the tail of tied regulation games in including-OT contracts.
A calibrated rating prior stabilises game-level estimates.
Market price and its moves after goalie/lineup news are the benchmark to beat.
Whether OT/SO counts defines the contract.
De-vigged sharp lines are a strong competing probability estimate.
Home last change steers matchups and slightly boosts the home team beyond generic home ice.
Replacement-level depth quality when regulars are out changes the lineup-adjusted team rating.
Spread and depth decide whether a modelled edge survives execution costs.
Price-dependent fees set the breakeven probability for the edge.
Trade flow around goalie confirmation shows speed and direction of information incorporation.
Settlement values calibrate the model and expose OT/SO and correction edge cases.

interactions.hypothesis: Goalie quality matters most against high-danger-shot teams: the effect of a starter switch should be modelled as GSAx times the opponent's expected shot-danger volume, not a constant.
Back-to-back fatigue interacts with starter rotation: the net effect of a back-to-back is mostly the backup goalie, so the flag should be conditioned on confirmed starter.
Regression of PDO should be partial: teams whose xG-implied finishing and goalie talent justify higher SH%/SV% should regress less.

game_side.mechanism: Win probability is driven by the difference in team goal-scoring and goal-prevention quality (xG-based, goalie-adjusted), shifted by home ice, rest and lineup/goalie news, and then mapped onto a settlement rule: including overtime and shootout the outcome is nearly 50/50 conditional on a regulation tie, while regulation-only and margin contracts depend on the goal-difference distribution.
game_side.target: Which team wins (regulation or including OT/SO per the contract wording), by margin or puck-line spread where applicable.

inputs.why: Combined shot-attempt volume sets the number of chances available.
Quality of chances each team creates scales total expected goals.
Opponent suppression quality caps or expands scoring.
Starting goalie quality changes goals against by large amounts game to game.
Convert shot quality to goals; needs shrinkage.
Expected power-play minutes add high-yield scoring time.
PP/PK efficiency converts penalty minutes into goals.
EN goals add to totals when games are close late.
Crew tendencies change penalties called, shifting PP opportunities.
Tired teams and backup goalies raise scoring.
Tail rungs price dispersion not just the mean.
Rink scoring environment and shot counting bias.
Threshold rungs reveal market's implied distribution.
Whether OT, SO goal, EN goal count for totals.
Trade flow after goalie confirmation indicates how the market re-priced totals.
Thin depth on total rungs affects executable edge.

interactions.hypothesis: Pace and goalie quality combine multiplicatively: high-event games with weak goalies produce fat right tails, high-event games with strong goalies mostly add saves not goals.
Penalty expectation is the product of team taken/drawn rates, crew tendency and PP efficiency; each alone overstates the effect.
EN goals are concentrated in games decided by one goal late; interacting spread with coach pull timing gives their expected contribution to the total.

game_total.mechanism: Goals are a function of shot volume, shot quality, goalie conversion and special-teams time for each team; totals are the sum of two overdispersed count processes with a small positive correlation through pace and empty-net goals. Inputs that change the number or quality of chances (pace, xG, goalies, penalty expectation) shift the mean, while script and EN dynamics shape the tail.
game_total.target: Total goals (or one team's goals) in regulation or the full game as defined by the contract, including empty-net goals; and both-teams-to-score style thresholds.

inputs.why: Expected SOG faced from team-level shot suppression.
Opponent shot creation volume and quality.
Total event volume of the game is the base for the number of shots the goalie can face.
Eligibility: market settlement depends on goalie playing.
Backup/starter probability and rest.
An early pull truncates the saves count and creates a lower tail not captured by a mean model.
Trailing opponents shoot more.
Win probability tilts shot volume.
PP chances for the opponent raise shots.
Official SOG counting bias at the rink moves the number of saves credited directly.
Opponent shooting by player mix.
Higher quality reduces goals and increases saves for given shots.
Shots faced are overdispersed; rung probabilities need a calibrated count distribution, not a mean.
Void/settlement rules when goalie does not start or is pulled.
First goalie off the ice at morning skate is a pregame tell for the starter and thus eligibility.

interactions.hypothesis: Saves distribution is a mixture over starter identity and pull events: P(starter) x saves distribution given starter, with pull risk truncating the upper tail.
Opponent SOG volume depends on game script: strong favourite goalies face fewer shots when team leads, so win probability interacts with shot volume against.
Special teams matter via both PP shots against and PK blocking: the penalties interaction with opponent PP shot volume shifts saves.

goalie_saves.mechanism: Saves = shots on goal faced minus goals allowed. Shots faced are determined by the opponent's attempts and SOG rates against this defence, with score-state effects (trailing team shoots more); goals allowed lower saves slightly. Early pulls truncate counts. Mean is driven by opposing volume and shot environment, variance by script and pull risk.
goalie_saves.target: Goalie saves in a game (threshold ladder), requiring the goalie to play, settled on official save counts.

inputs.why: Reference-class frequency of the same type of announcement is the best available prior for novelty markets.
Fixed league dates bound when the event can occur and concentrate hazard near them.
Insider reports often precede official announcements; timing and reliability of reports drive repricing.
Resolution wording and source.
Market-implied probability and news timing.
Thin liquidity means the quoted probability is noisy and sparse trading limits the value of any signal.
Market open/close timing relative to events.
Other venue prices where they exist.

interactions.hypothesis: Base rate adjusted by calendar: probability concentrates in dated windows, so reference-class frequency interacts with time to deadline.
Insider-report timing leads official announcement; price reaction after reports shows information content and the rule defines what counts.

off_field.mechanism: These markets depend on organizational decisions and news flow rather than on-ice performance; there is no strong statistical model, so the best hypotheses are reference-class frequencies, calendar constraints, insider reports and the exact resolution wording. Largely unpredictable from hockey statistics.
off_field.target: Non-game events (trades, coaching, league announcements, business or non-hockey questions) settled by public announcement.

inputs.why: Period-specific scoring and shot shape for each team.
Chance quality creation per 20 minutes.
Chance suppression per 20 minutes.
Goalie identity drives period goals against; warm-up matters in period one.
Third-period behaviour depends on lead/trail state.
PP chances concentrate in particular periods.
Line deployment per period (top lines early).
Second-period change dynamics.
Late third-period EN goals matter for third-period totals.
Whether period markets include OT or only regulation periods.

interactions.hypothesis: First-period goals depend on opening deployments and goalie state; interacting opening shift lines with starting goalie quality is more informative than team-level rates.
Third-period totals and winners depend on game-script mixture: probability of being tied or trailing late times pull timing.
Second-period outcomes combine long-change effect with team skating depth and line shuffle tendencies.

period.mechanism: Period outcomes are small-sample versions of the full-game process with period-specific shapes: first periods are cagier, second periods have long changes, third periods are dominated by score effects and empty-net goals. With ties common (period winner can tie), the distribution is heavily discrete and sensitive to the goalie and the first-minutes deployment.
period.target: Winner, goal total, spread or both-teams-score within a single period (1st, 2nd or 3rd).

inputs.why: Relative minutes of the two players.
Per-60 rates drive comparison for shot markets.
Relative PP roles decide which player collects the high-yield minutes that separate two similar skaters.
Linemates and deployment differences.
Difference in chance quality gives the expected gap in goals/points between the two players.
Differential opponent suppression.
Correlation shapes the difference distribution.
Lineup availability for either player.
If either player is scratched the comparison may void or settle against him depending on the wording.
Tie and DNP rules for the comparison.

interactions.hypothesis: For teammates, correlation via shared game script reduces variance of the difference; for opponents, scripts can produce negatively correlated shot volumes.
Difference of expected points depends on both players' PP roles and the opponent's penalty exposure, so PP minute distribution interacts with role.

player_other.mechanism: A head-to-head comparison is the difference of two correlated count processes: each player's expected output given role and matchup, with correlation from shared game environment (both on the same team or opposing teams) and tie handling defined by the rule. The distribution of the difference is wider than either marginal alone and tie/push rules matter.
player_other.target: Head-to-head player comparisons (who records more points/shots) and other non-standard player markets.

inputs.why: TOI by state is the volume multiplier.
PP1 slot drives a disproportionate share of points.
Linemates define who converts passes and shoots.
Shot-quality-based scoring baseline for goals.
Individual shot volume for goal probability.
Playmaking role for assist markets.
Persistent finishing skill after regression.
On-ice conversion luck for assist and point projection.
Linemate finishing quality for assists and points.
Opposing goalie quality affects conversion rates.
Opponent suppression by position.
Lineup news changes linemates and PP roles.
If the player is scratched the contract may void rather than lose, which changes the price of a pregame position.
Count distribution for thresholds.
Correlated rungs on the player's ladder.
Returning players often carry reduced minutes and altered PP roles in their first games back.
Morning-skate lines and PP units arrive before official lineups and shift role expectations.
Matchup deployment against shutdown lines changes a star player scoring opportunities at home or away.

interactions.hypothesis: Points per game scale with TOI by state times per-minute rate: PP minutes and EV minutes need separate rates and the PP slot interacts with opponent PK structure.
Assist projection should use linemates' ixG-based finishing rather than realised on-ice SH%, because on-ice luck regresses.
A starting goalie change shifts every skater's goal probability, so the opposing goalie interacts with the player's ixG baseline.

player_points.mechanism: Points are rare events driven by the number of chances a player is on the ice for (TOI by strength state), the shooter/passer role on those chances (PP unit slot, linemates), the quality of those chances (xG), conversion luck, and the opponent's goal prevention including the starting goalie. Distribution is highly discrete and overdispersed, with most mass at 0 and a thin tail, so role and TOI information and regression of luck dominate.
player_points.target: Player goals, assists or points (thresholds like 1+ or 2+ points) in a game, with possible void on DNP.

inputs.why: Individual SOG rate per 60 is the central skill.
Minutes by state multiply shot rate.
PP time yields high shot rates for shooters.
Attempt-to-SOG conversion by shooter and opponent.
Opponent's shots allowed by position.
Opponent team shots volume allowed.
Rink scorer bias for SOG counting.
Trailing and leading change shot volume.
Probability of being in trailing states.
Linemates and zone deployment set how many attempts the player gets per shift.
A teammate's absence promotes the player to PP1 or a top line, raising shot volume sharply.
Defencemen shot counts come from point shots and PP time, with different volume and block rates than forwards.
Distribution for rung probabilities.
Correlated shot rungs for same player.
Call-ups change line composition and PP units, changing shot opportunities for regulars.
Returning players have reduced TOI so shots are below baseline for early games back.

interactions.hypothesis: SOG rate per minute depends on strength state: expected SOG is EV TOI x EV rate + PP TOI x PP rate, and projected PP TOI itself depends on penalty rates and crew.
Opponent block rate converts attempts into SOG differently for defencemen at the point and for forwards in the slot.
Trailing script raises shot volume for the underdog's stars and lowers favourites' late shots, so pregame win probability interacts with player TOI and shot rate.

player_shots.mechanism: SOG = TOI by strength state x attempts per minute x share of attempts reaching the net. Role (D vs F, PP slot, shooting-first players), game script (score effects), opponent block/suppression and rink counting bias determine the mean; variance is high because both TOI and shot rate fluctuate, and thresholds at 2-4 SOG fall in the dense part of the distribution.
player_shots.target: Player shots on goal in a game (threshold ladder), settled on official SOG counts.

inputs.why: Counting stats and advanced metrics voters see.
Who votes, how many ballot slots and when ballots are cast determine which information can matter.
Team success correlates with winning.
Goalie awards depend on save percentage and workload.
Narrative around rookies and age curves influence voters for Calder and comeback-style awards.
Games played and late injuries.
Late narrative events (injury, milestone, scandal) can swing voters, especially before ballot deadlines.
Finalist announcements and the award date define when information resolves and when markets can close.

interactions.hypothesis: Voter models combine production rank and team rank: a candidate on a high-seeded team with top-two production has a higher chance than raw rank implies.
Finalist announcements and ballot deadlines create step changes: late-season injuries after ballots close do not affect votes.

season_award.mechanism: Award outcomes are a mixture of measurable production and voter narrative, filtered through ballot structure and timing; the best predictor is a voter-behaviour model fit on historical finalists with stats, team success and position. Late-season injuries and finalist announcements are discrete information events.
season_award.target: Winners (or finalists) of league awards such as Hart, Vezina, Norris, Calder, Selke, Conn Smythe, decided by voters.

inputs.why: Calibrated team strength with uncertainty.
Process-based offence component of ratings.
Process-based defence component.
Goalie is the largest single-player driver, especially in playoffs.
Long-term injuries to stars change strength.
Remaining schedule difficulty and games in hand.
Qualification and seeding in tight races are decided by formal tie-break order, not raw points.
Series state for playoff series markets.
Lucky shooting/save runs inflate standings; regress before simulating the rest of the season.
Playoff-specific TOI and penalty environment.
Trades, coaching changes and signings shift team strength after public ratings were fitted.
Sportsbook futures prices are a benchmark for rating-based probabilities and show the market's information.

interactions.hypothesis: Playoff odds depend on rating uncertainty: with the same mean strength, higher uncertainty helps underdogs in short series; simulate with correlated rating errors.
Goalie quality is the most volatile determinant in playoffs; a goalie change interacts with the process rating to move series odds more than skater changes.
Standing luck (PDO and OT record) mean-reverts, but qualification depends on the tie-break structure, so regress then apply formal rules.

season_outcome.mechanism: These markets integrate team strength over many games or a short series: probability is the result of a simulation using team ratings with their uncertainty, injuries, schedule, tiebreakers and bracket structure. Futures are heavily influenced by rating uncertainty and by information that arrives slowly (injuries, trades), and hold time of capital matters.
season_outcome.target: Season-level outcomes: championship, conference/division titles, playoff qualification, playoff series winners.

inputs.why: To-date totals and rest-of-season projection.
A recent TOI or role change shifts the rest-of-season rate before season totals reveal it.
PP role is a stable scoring driver.
Chance-quality baseline separates sustainable production from finishing luck in the rest-of-season rate.
Hot shooting that exceeds skill regresses, lowering the rest-of-season projection for current leaders.
Games missed to injury directly reduce totals and change leader probabilities.
Age curve gives a prior for rate changes and for the injury hazard over the remaining season.
Games remaining and opponent quality set opportunity count and chance quality for the rest of the season.
Distribution of totals for thresholds.
Trades or role changes alter opportunity and linemates for the player mid-season.

interactions.hypothesis: Projected total = games remaining x health probability x per-game rate; the injury hazard interacts with age and workload.
Leader races are decided by top-tail variance of rate and by role stability, so TOI trend interacts with PP role.

season_stat.mechanism: Cumulative stats equal rate x opportunity: rest-of-season per-game production times expected games played, with health risk and role changes. Leader markets also depend on competitors' paths and the top-tail variance of counts.
season_stat.target: Season-total or leader outcomes for players or teams (goals, points, saves, wins), settled at end of season or on specified date.

m.ladder_structure.label: Cross-rung consistency of the threshold ladder (monotonicity, implied distribution)
m.ladder_structure.measurement: For each event/player collect all live rungs at one timestamp; check P(k) non-increasing; fit a discrete distribution (Poisson, negative binomial, or free-form isotonic) to mid prices; compare implied mean/variance and per-rung residual to the model; track which rungs the market lags when news arrives.
m.ladder_structure.mechanism: Rungs of a threshold ladder (e.g. 4+, 5+, 6+) must imply one coherent count distribution; deviations expose stale or mispriced rungs and reveal the market's implied mean and variance.
m.ladder_structure.rationale: Ladders for the same player/game are strongly correlated, so edges on adjacent rungs are not independent bets and exposure must be sized per ladder. Subtle: because each rung is a survival probability P(X>=k), monotone non-increasing is a hard constraint, and fitting a Poisson/negative-binomial to the rungs gives an implied mean that can be compared to a model mean on a like-for-like basis.

Shrink team hazard to league with k=150 PP opportunities and 2-season half-life. Expected PP goals = sum over expected penalties of integral hazard x survival; keep major and double-minor cases separate.
nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.mechanism: Expected PP goals per penalty given that a minor ends on a goal and PP1/PP2 share the clock.
nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.rationale: PP time is not additive: a two-minute minor ends when the power-play team scores, so goals per PP are concave in minutes, and the first unit plays roughly the first 60-80 seconds, so PP1 production dominates short power plays. Using PP time x rate overstates multi-goal PP games and misallocates credit among players.

nhl.toi.label: Projected time on ice by strength state (EV, PP, PK, late-game)
nhl.toi.measurement: Rolling EWMA TOI per strength state (last 10-20 games) conditioned on lineup (who is in/out), with adjustments for expected penalties and expected score script; model TOI by state as separate counts then sum; record projected-vs-actual error.
nhl.toi.mechanism: TOI by situation is the volume multiplier for every counting stat: more minutes (especially PP) means more shots, points and saves opportunities.
nhl.toi.rationale: Individual shots, points and assists scale nearly linearly with TOI; the key is the split by strength state because PP minutes are worth much more per minute than EV minutes. Subtle: TOI is partly endogenous to the score (stars play more when trailing), to penalties drawn and to coach decisions, so a pregame projection must be from the specific lineup and expected game script, not season average.

nhl.total_goal_dispersion.label: Goal-total dispersion and home/away goal correlation (incl. empty-net contribution)
nhl.total_goal_dispersion.measurement: Fit negative-binomial or bivariate Poisson to team-game goals with covariates; estimate overdispersion and correlation by season; backtest calibration of tail rungs.
nhl.total_goal_dispersion.mechanism: Total-goal outcomes are more dispersed than Poisson because of score effects, special teams and empty-net goals, and home/away goals are weakly correlated.
nhl.total_goal_dispersion.rationale: Threshold probabilities on total/team total depend on the variance and correlation, not just the mean. Subtle: dispersion differs by environment (high-event vs low-event teams), and quarter-point style ladders mean the tail rungs are pricing dispersion.

nhl.venue.label: Rink effects (shot counting bias), home advantage, building specifics
nhl.venue.measurement: Estimate venue-specific shot-count multipliers via fixed-effects model on visiting teams' SOG per 60 across venues; use team-venue-season random effect; add home-ice indicator and altitude (Denver, Utah) as controls.
nhl.venue.mechanism: Different arenas record shots, hits and takeaways at different rates, and home teams see small advantages (last change, crowd, referees).
nhl.venue.rationale: Rink scorer bias inflates or deflates shot and SOG counts by arena; since SOG props settle on official counts, this is a pure measurement effect worth several percent. Subtle: bias is estimated from visiting teams' stats across venues and shifts with scorer turnover, and home advantage in hockey is modest and partly driven by last-change matchups.

nhl.xg_against.label: Team expected goals against (shot suppression quality)
nhl.xg_against.measurement: Per-60 xGA at 5v5 and on PK, score/venue-adjusted, exponentially weighted with opponent adjustment via the same ridge team-effects model as xG for; recompute with lineup-weighted projection (replace absent defencemen with replacement-level impact) for the specific game.
nhl.xg_against.mechanism: Expected goals against measure the quality and quantity of chances a team's skaters allow, independent of whether the goalie happened to stop them.
nhl.xg_against.rationale: Separates defensive process (what the skaters control) from goaltending outcome; critical for totals, team totals and for estimating what shot quality a goalie will face. Subtle: xGA as published is goalie-neutral, so any goalie-specific adjustment must be layered on top, and defensive effects partly reflect personnel (injuries to top pair) that stale season averages hide.

nhl.xg_for.label: Team expected goals for (shot quality created), strength-split and adjusted
nhl.xg_for.measurement: Per-60 xGF at 5v5 (score-and-venue adjusted) and on PP, as exponentially weighted averages (half-life ~25-40 games) shrunk toward league mean with a prior sized by games played; adjust for opponent by regressing team-game xGF on offence and defence team effects plus home indicator (ridge). Report separate 5v5 and special-teams components rather than one blended number.
nhl.xg_for.mechanism: Expected goals credit the quality and location of shots a team generates, so xGF measures offensive process with far less shooting-luck noise than goals.
nhl.xg_for.rationale: Goals are rare and luck-heavy; xG stabilises much faster and is the best public repeatable measure of offence. Subtle: public xG models omit passing/pre-shot movement and goalie quality, treat all shooters equally, and are biased by rink scorer inconsistency in shot location. Use it split by 5v5 / PP and adjust for opponent and for score effects, since trailing teams inflate volume.

draft_selection.label: NHL draft selections (top pick and draft slot)
draft_selection.mechanism: Draft order comes from two institutional pieces: slots 1-16 from the standings-weighted lottery among non-playoff clubs, slots 17-32 from playoff results, then pick ownership maps each slot to a club. Clubs choose sequentially from a shrinking board, so whether a named prospect lands at slot k depends on who was taken at slots 1..k-1; consensus is tight at the top and loose mid-round, where club need, general-manager habit, medical flags and late trades decide. Kalshi settles on the player and the overall slot, not on the club.
draft_selection.target: Whether a named prospect is selected at an exact overall slot, or within the top N overall slots, of the NHL Draft; determined by lottery and playoff-based draft order, pick ownership and sequential club choices.

inputs.why: Live series state (score, games played, home ice, rest, lineup) determines how many games remain and the goals already banked.
Model output, not data: the joint winner-by-length pmf computed from ratings, goalies, venue and the dependence parameter; it maps directly to games, score and spread settlement.
Team strength gap determines per-game win probability and so series length and, through goal means, per-game scoring.
The goaltender is the largest controllable driver of both goals against and series length in the playoffs.
Per-game goal totals are overdispersed with home-away correlation; the series sum inherits that dispersion.
Playoff scoring runs lower than the regular season with fewer penalties and continuous overtime; this fixes the per-game goal mean.
Trailing, elimination and game-seven states shift the per-game goal rate in ways the series score reveals.
Adjustments across the series change scoring by game index, which matters for later games in a long series.
Shot-quality creation sets team goal means with less noise than raw goals.
Shot-quality suppression sets the opponent's goal mean and the series total.
Goaltending variance beyond binomial changes how lopsided individual games are; the direction of its effect on length depends on which side's goalie runs hot.
Attempts per 60 for the pair controls shots and so goals, and drops in playoff matchups.
Power-play and penalty-kill matchups produce a share of playoff goals despite fewer penalties.
Penalty frequency determines power-play opportunities, a large source of variance in goals.
Injuries to stars and goalies mid-series change per-game strength and thus length and goals.
Explicit state-conditional empty-net module; dispersion is then fitted on non-empty-net goals so empty-net goals are not counted twice.
The year-level scoring level recalibrates the goal mean of every game.
Probability a game is tied after regulation decides how often a game adds exactly one OT goal and is the per-game rate for the series OT-count contract.
Beta-binomial overdispersion of OT-game counts within a series sets the tail for 'at least k games go to overtime' strikes.
Uncertainty in the pair's strength differential is shared by every game; averaging over it makes series more lopsided (shorter) and moves the winner-by-length cells.
Playoff starter changes after a bad game shift per-game goals and win probability for the remaining games of the series.
Days between playoff games vary from one to three or more, and cross-country travel within a series changes per-game strength.
Which matchups occur in later rounds drives the championship exact-score market listed before the Final and the league-wide comeback event.
Fitted sign and size of game-to-game dependence within a series; the only data-estimated quantity behind the length pmf beyond per-game probabilities.
Win probability of a team facing elimination or trailing 0-3 differs from its pre-series rate, which drives comeback and 7-game probabilities.
An error in the pair's combined scoring level is shared by every game, so series-total variance grows with games squared; the strength-differential posterior does not carry it.

interactions.hypothesis: Uncertainty about the strength gap is shared by all games: averaging the length pmf over the rating posterior lowers expected length and the game-7 share near parity.
A hot favourite goalie shortens the series and lowers goals per game (both reduce the total); a hot underdog goalie lowers goals per game but lengthens the series, so the effects on the total offset.
Empty-net goals concentrate in late one-goal deficits of elimination games, so their contribution to series goals depends on series state.

The OT-game count is a beta-binomial over games played with per-game rate from the tie model; closely matched pairs have both higher tie rates and longer series, so the count's tail rises faster than either alone.
A 0-3 comeback needs four straight wins by the trailing team; its probability depends on the trailing team's state-shifted win rate compounded by the sign of game-to-game dependence.

Shared scoring-level uncertainty adds variance proportional to games squared, so it widens total-goal tails most for evenly rated pairs that play long series and least for mismatches that end in four or five.
Expected length and P(game 7) are concave in per-game win probability near parity, so integrating over the strength-differential posterior lowers both and moves mass to sweeps and five-game series.

A hot favourite goalie both shortens the series and lowers goals per game, so both channels cut the total; a hot underdog goalie lowers goals per game but lengthens the series, so the channels offset. The interaction is conditional on which side's goalie deviates.

Empty-net goals are rare in neutral states but common when a team trails by one late in an elimination game; the empty-net contribution to goals is concentrated in the elimination states, so its effect depends on series state.

OT-game count is beta-binomial over games played with per-game rate from the tie model; evenly matched pairs have higher tie rates and longer series at once, so the upper tail of the count (5+ OT games) rises much faster than either factor alone.
Early games reflect the regular-season matchup, while later games reflect adjustment and heavier playoff structure (fewer penalties, tighter checking); scoring drifts between regimes by game index.

A 0-3 comeback is four consecutive wins by the trailing team: the per-game state-shifted win rate is raised to the fourth power, and any bounce-back dependence multiplies each step, so small shifts compound strongly.

The shared scoring-level error enters every game, so its contribution to the variance of series goals is its variance times games squared; length is longest for evenly rated pairs, so the same uncertainty widens total-goal tails far more for close matchups than for mismatches.

playoff_series_aggregate.label: NHL playoff series aggregate outcomes (series total goals, length, exact score, game spread, OT count, 3-0 comeback)
playoff_series_aggregate.mechanism: Per-game win probabilities from team ratings (with shared posterior uncertainty), goaltending and the 2-2-1-1-1 home pattern give the joint winner-by-length pmf that settles series games, exact score, game spread and championship score. Series total goals add per-game scoring, lowered by the playoff environment and shifted by series state, with every regulation tie adding exactly one sudden-death goal. The OT-game count uses regulation-tie probability with within-series dependence. The league-wide 0-3 comeback event aggregates the path probability over the bracket.
playoff_series_aggregate.target: A quantity defined over a whole best-of-7 playoff series (total goals, games played, exact winner-and-length score, margin in games, count of overtime games), or a path event across all series of one postseason (any 0-3 comeback). Each depends on the joint distribution of the winner and length (4-7 games) and, for goals and OT, on per-game scoring and ties.
